issues.description: simulate_msd_two_rounds has a signature mismatch between the problem statement/solution and the template. The problem statement specifies `simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots:int, p: float, batch_size:int = 1000000)` (needed for batching), and the solution implements `batch_size`. The template omits `batch_size`, so students following the prompt cannot implement batching without changing the template API (likely breaking tests expecting the documented signature).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `def simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: int = 1000000) -> tuple[float, float]:` and ensure the docstring includes the `batch_size` parameter.

issues.description: inject has a parameter annotation mismatch: the problem statement specifies `inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit) -> int` with `injection_qubit` implied to be an int (a qubit index). The template and solution omit the type annotation for `injection_qubit`, which is inconsistent with the rest of the typed API presented in the prompt and can confuse students about the intended input type.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the missing type annotation in template (and optionally solution) for clarity: `def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int:`.

issues.description: build_msd_circ return-value description is inconsistent with the problem statement. The problem statement says the second returned list must be the measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (ordered by qubit). The template docstring instead claims the second list is the final X-basis measurements of the distilled state, which misidentifies what the indices refer to and can mislead students when implementing error detection/post-processing.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template docstring (and, if desired, the solution docstring) so the second returned list is described as: "measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (ordered by qubit index)".

issues.description: correct_teleportation semantics are described inconsistently. The problem statement defines it as returning an array of corrections (0 = don't flip X measurement, 1 = flip). The template docstring instead says it returns "corrected measurements", and the solution returns `teleportation_measurements ^ x_measurements`, which is a derived bit array but not explicitly labeled as "corrections" vs "corrected outcomes". This ambiguity affects later tasks where students must apply the correction to X-basis measurement results.
issues.suggestedFix: Pick one interpretation and align all artifacts. Recommended: treat the function output as the correction bitmask; update the template docstring (and optionally rename local variables in the solution) to state it returns correction bits to XOR into the X-basis measurement results.
